title: Finiteness over every nonconstant analytic parameter
statement: Let $k\subseteq E$ be complete fields with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values, with $k$ algebraically closed [def-weil-field]. For any such field $F$ put $F^\circ=\{a:|a|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\{a:|a|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_F=|F^\times|\subset\mathbf R_{>0}$. For $z\in E$ write $k(z)^\wedge$ for the closure of the subfield generated by $k$ and $z$. Assume $E\ne k$ and $E$ is finite over $k(y)^\wedge$ for some $y\in E$. For every $z\in E\setminus k$, the field extension $E/k(z)^\wedge$ is finite.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, printed pp. 48–49, specialized to algebraically closed ground field.

proof.text:
Put $F=k(y)^\wedge$. Necessarily $y
otin k$: otherwise $F=k$ and finite $E/k$ contradicts algebraic closedness and $E
e k$. Fix $z
otin k$. Let $H$ be the relative separable closure of $F$ in $E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable], $H/F$ is separable and $E/H$ is purely inseparable. Both extensions are finite, since any linearly independent subset over an intermediate field is bounded in size by $[E:F]$. In characteristic zero put $x=z$; in characteristic $p>0$ choose $n$ with $x=z^{p^n}\in H$. In either case $x
otin k$: a polynomial $T^{p^n}-x$ with $x\in k$ would force $z\in k$ by algebraic closedness (in characteristic zero this is immediate). By [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-subspace-closed], the finite-dimensional $F$-subspace $H$ of $E$ is closed, hence complete. The same lemma with scalars $k$ shows that $k$ is closed in $E$, so $r=\inf_{a\in k}|x-a|>0$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, p. 49, separable reduction; explicit completeness and distance checks.

proof.text: The rational subfield $D=k(y)$ is dense in $F$ by its definition. Apply [lem-trf-dense-subfield-separable-descent] to $D\subseteq F\subseteq H$, obtaining a finite separable extension $l/D$ inside $H$ which is dense in $H$. Choose $x^\prime\in l$ with $|x-x^\prime|<r/4$. It cannot lie in $k$, since every $a\in k$ satisfies $|x-a|\geq r$. Both $y$ and $x^\prime$ are transcendental over $k$: every element algebraic over an algebraically closed field belongs to that field.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, p. 49, algebraic dense model and parameter approximation.

proof.text: The extension $l/k$ is finitely generated, since $l/k(y)$ is finite; a basis over $k(y)$ together with $y$ generates it as a field. The transcendence-degree tower formula [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k l=1$, because $y$ is transcendental and $l/k(y)$ is algebraic. Likewise $k(x^\prime)/k$ is finitely generated of transcendence degree one. Apply the last clause of [lem-sfb-curve-function-field-arithmetic] to the inclusion $k(x^\prime)\subseteq l$: $[l:k(x^\prime)]<\infty$. Now [lem-trf-valued-decompletion-etale], its first clause only, gives $[H:K^\prime]<\infty$ for $K^\prime=k(x^\prime)^\wedge$, since $H$ is precisely the completion of its dense subfield $l$ and $K^\prime$ is the closure of $k(x^\prime)$ in $H$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, p. 49, final algebraic function-field degree and completion bound.

proof.text: Put $K=k(x)^\wedge$. Since $H$ is closed in $E$ and contains $x$, this closure is contained in $H$. Apply [lem-trf-nearby-parameter-isometric-substitution] in $H$ with $u=x$, $v=x^\prime$ and $c=1/4$. It gives an isometric $k$-isomorphism $\phi:K\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\prime$ with $|b-\phi(b)|\leq|b|/4$. Use [lem-trf-analytic-close-embedding-degree] with its domain $K$, ambient field $H$, first embedding the composite of $\phi$ with $K^\prime\hookrightarrow H$, and second embedding the inclusion $K\hookrightarrow H$. The first image has finite index by Step 3; therefore the second also does, and $[H:K]=[H:K^\prime]<\infty$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, p. 49, application of the two preceding lemmas, in the orientation with the already finite image first.

proof.text: Finally $[E:H]<\infty$ from Step 1 and $[H:K]<\infty$ from Step 4 imply $[E:K]<\infty$: products of finite spanning sets span $E$ over $K$. Because $x=z$ or $x=z^{p^n}$, one has $k(x)\subseteq k(z)$ and hence $K\subseteq k(z)^\wedge\subseteq E$. The same finite $K$-spanning set of $E$ spans over the larger scalar field $k(z)^\wedge$. Thus $[E:k(z)^\wedge]<\infty$, as required for the arbitrary $z\notin k$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, p. 49, reversal of the separable reduction; finite spanning-set argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q98-1c9849c77 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, both new nodes and every cited statement in full. The local literature has no Temkin file, so I read arXiv:0707.3953v3 §6.3 (Lemmas 6.3.2–6.3.3, Cor. 6.3.4 and its proof, Rem. 6.3.5, printed pp. 48–49) from a local text copy of the same version. The five steps follow the proof of 6.3.4 in order: separable reduction with a p-power of z; Krasner descent to a dense l/k(y); a nearby x' in l; the algebraic degree [l:k(x')] < ∞ from the transcendence-degree tower and the last generic clause of sfb-curve-function-field-arithmetic; the completed degree bound from the first clause of valued-decompletion-etale; the 6.3.2 substitution followed by close-embedding-degree, with the already-finite image put first (that node's hypothesis direction, checked); then an elementary tower argument. Hypotheses checked: H is complete because a finite-dimensional subspace is closed; k is closed so r>0; x and x' are not in k; y and x' are transcendental; c=1/4. dense-subfield-separable-descent is true: approximate the separable minimal polynomial over dense D, then Krasner over complete F, then density through equivalent norms. Tested on H=F, D=F and char p. It is not a duplicate: the DVR completion approximation, the dense-henselian comparison and the Krasner nodes all differ. nearby-parameter-isometric-substitution is Lemma 6.3.2 with k algebraically closed and a closed bound; it is true by factoring over k, relative errors under products and inverses, and limits. It is not a duplicate: the same argument appears only inline in the downstream lem-trf-analytic-uniformization, which would be cyclic to cite. Both new nodes are statement-only, self-contained, searched with all three kinds and strictly smaller than the item. The item statement is unchanged.
